from solution import sort_counter


def test_issue_example():
    """Example sorts by value as [('Chemistry', 87), ('Physics', 83), ('Math', 81)]."""
    # 87 > 83 > 81 so Chemistry first, Physics second, Math last
    expected = [('Chemistry', 87), ('Physics', 83), ('Math', 81)]
    assert sort_counter({'Math': 81, 'Physics': 83, 'Chemistry': 87}) == expected


def test_issue_empty():
    """Sort counter by value handles empty input."""
    # 0 entries in so 0 entries out
    expected = []
    assert sort_counter({}) == expected


def test_issue_single_entry():
    """Sort counter by value handles a single entry."""
    # only one value 10 so no reordering needed
    expected = [('Math', 10)]
    assert sort_counter({'Math': 10}) == expected


def test_issue_ascending_becomes_descending():
    """Sort counter by value puts largest value first."""
    # 3 > 2 > 1 so c first, b second, a last
    expected = [('c', 3), ('b', 2), ('a', 1)]
    assert sort_counter({'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 3}) == expected


def test_issue_already_descending():
    """Sort counter by value keeps descending input in order."""
    # 30 > 20 > 10 so x first, y second, z last
    expected = [('x', 30), ('y', 20), ('z', 10)]
    assert sort_counter({'x': 30, 'y': 20, 'z': 10}) == expected


def test_issue_negative_values():
    """Sort counter by value orders negative values descending."""
    # -1 > -5 > -10 so b first, a second, c last
    expected = [('b', -1), ('a', -5), ('c', -10)]
    assert sort_counter({'a': -5, 'b': -1, 'c': -10}) == expected


def test_issue_zero_and_positive():
    """Sort counter by value handles zero boundary correctly."""
    # 5 > 0 > -2 so b first, a second, c last
    expected = [('b', 5), ('a', 0), ('c', -2)]
    assert sort_counter({'a': 0, 'b': 5, 'c': -2}) == expected


def test_issue_float_values():
    """Sort counter by value orders float values descending."""
    # 2.25 > 1.5 > 0.75 so b first, a second, c last
    expected = [('b', 2.25), ('a', 1.5), ('c', 0.75)]
    assert sort_counter({'a': 1.5, 'b': 2.25, 'c': 0.75}) == expected


def test_issue_equal_values():
    """Sort counter by value keeps all entries when values tie."""
    # 90 == 90 > 80 so a and b tie for first, c last
    expected_set = {('a', 90), ('b', 90), ('c', 80)}
    assert set(sort_counter({'a': 90, 'b': 90, 'c': 80})) == expected_set


def test_issue_five_entries():
    """Sort counter by value orders five entries descending."""
    # 90 > 87 > 83 > 81 > 75 so English, Chemistry, Physics, Math, Biology
    expected = [('English', 90), ('Chemistry', 87), ('Physics', 83), ('Math', 81), ('Biology', 75)]
    assert sort_counter({'Math': 81, 'Physics': 83, 'Chemistry': 87, 'Biology': 75, 'English': 90}) == expected


def test_contract_returns_list():
    """Example shows sort_counter result is a list."""
    # 2 > 1 so b first, a last; result must be a list
    result = sort_counter({'a': 1, 'b': 2})
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_contract_returns_tuples():
    """Example shows sort_counter result elements are tuples."""
    # 2 > 1 so b first, a last; each element must be a tuple pair
    result = sort_counter({'a': 1, 'b': 2})
    assert all(isinstance(item, tuple) and len(item) == 2 for item in result)
